speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are presenting with gait and limb ataxia; let's begin by asking: have you noticed any recent onset of double vision, slurred speech, or weakness on one side of your body?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient confirms progressive gait and limb ataxia, specifically noting clumsiness on the right side. Given the laterality and the nature of the symptoms, I need to determine if there are any associated cerebellar signs like nystagmus or dysmetria, and check for any past neurological events.

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)

Your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab puts you at high risk for JC virus reactivation. Although you asked for a specific diagnosis, the clinical picture strongly suggests PML rather than Multiple Sclerosis, which is why I ordered the MRI immediately.
